brief: Goldman's CoT read: Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling continued through September 29th, with $10.5bn sold September 22-29, the 5th selling week of the past 6 since August 18th, for a cumulative net of -$63.7bn. Asset Manager led (sold $11.7bn, Other sold $1.1bn) while Hedge Fund and Non-Reportable bought small amounts ($620mm, $1.6bn). Higher real rates and quarter-end rebalancing drove this: Asset Manager liquidation of $5.5bn coincided with a 25bp jump in 10-year real yields, and the rolling 3-month correlation between Asset Manager gross longs and real yields turned sharply negative. Separately, below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers, and a Nonfarm payrolls miss cut October hike odds, lifting the S&P 0.70%. But the December Adjusted Interest Rate future (a funding proxy) cheapened ~5bps, so GS still reads futures flows as bearish. Asset Manager net length sits at a 77% 2-year rank before additional likely sales, implying ongoing pressure until yields reverse convincingly. GS rates research nonetheless sees a skew toward lower yields, despite upward risk from oil and resilient AI capex.
